title: Introduce claimed-region assertions, KMS-fallback guardian, and RBAC v2 service endorsements
author: Asha Raman
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating in regulated regions asked for stronger per-request provenance and a safer KMS failover story when models are served across multi-region pools. This PR extends RBAC v2 to support transient 'service endorsements' (short-lived assertions that an operator or service has explicitly approved a non-default KMS provider for a request), introduces a KMS-fallback guardian that scores and selects fallback providers based on residency claims and operator policy, and emits an audit watermark that ties the selected KMS provider, claimed region, and endorsement decider into a single signed ledger entry. The goal is to improve both auditability and graceful degradation when regional keys are unavailable.

What this PR implements (high level):
- A new endorsements subsystem in services/authorization/rbac/v2 that allows services to register ephemeral endorsements (issuer, ttl, scope) and exposes a minimal API for endorsement lookup at request-time.
- A KMS-fallback guardian (pkg/kms/guardian) that evaluates requested key location, configured regional preferences, endorsement presence, and provider health signals to pick a primary provider or an auditable fallback.
- Audit watermarking (pkg/audit/watermark) that records a compact, monotonic watermark for requests that include claimed-region/KMS selection data; watermark entries are signed with the platform audit key and ingested by the audit pipeline.
- Migration layer and config flags: feature flag 'rbac_v2_endorsements' and 'kms_fallback_guardian' gate the rollout; a migration task upgrades existing policy caches to understand endorsement predicates.
- Telemetry and metrics: new histograms and counters for fallback decisions, endorsement hit-rate, and watermark emission latency.

Checklist (rollout plan):
- [x] Unit tests for endorsements rule engine and guardian decision logic
- [x] Integration test simulating region outage and fallback selection
- [x] Audit pipeline integration for watermark ingestion (staging)
- [x] Security review with threat scenarios and mitigations
- [x] Docs: added claimed-region authoring guide and operator runbook

Compatibility and safety notes: This is additive and behind feature flags. Default behavior remains unchanged. The endorsements API accepts signed assertions and will reject unsigned or expired assertions by default. Operators can opt into allowing unsigned—but logged—endorsements in non-prod to ease migration. There are no changes to default KMS selection unless the guardian flag is enabled.

Files touched and intent: small, focused changes to authorization and KMS selection, an audit shim, and Helm hooks to enable the guardian on a per-cluster basis. See files_changed below for specifics.

Related work and references: ENG-3124 (claimed-region strategy), SEC-147 (KMS provider hardening), SUP-8021 (customer support case that motivated fallback requirements). This PR references the residency contract introduced in docs/security/data-residency.md and expands the operator runbook in docs/ops/kms-fallback-runbook.md.

review_comments: Priya Kapoor: Request changes - please ensure endorsement cache eviction respects TTLs and add a test for cache staleness.
Asha Raman: Addressed - added eviction logic and a unit test that fast-forwards clock to exercise TTL expiry (see endorsements_test.go).

Dan Rodriguez: Question - how do we surface fallback reasons to customers? Reply: added structured audit watermark that includes a 'fallback_reason' enum and a telemetry tag (guardian.fallback_reason).

Mei Chen: Security review - tool indicates potential info leak if unsigned endorsements are allowed. Recommendation: require signed endorsements for production clusters. Patch updated to enforce by default and document opt-in for permissive mode.
Lucas Ortega: Approval - verified integration test reproduces region outage and recorded expected watermark entries. Approving for merge.
ci_checks: e2e-tests: passed (flaky on first run, passed on rerun)
security-scan: pass (low-risk findings; flagged permissive endorsement option; mitigation: default deny)
release_notes: Add optional RBAC v2 endorsements and a KMS-fallback guardian to improve auditable fallback behavior when regional KMS providers are unavailable. Feature is behind feature flags (rbac_v2_endorsements, kms_fallback_guardian). Adds watermark audit events and telemetry for fallback decisions.
notes_for_ops: Enable 'kms_fallback_guardian' gradually: start in staging with permissive endorsements false, run integration failure scenarios, then enable in a single region before global rollout. Provide platform audit key to watermark signer via KMS secret rotation. Monitor guardian.fallback_reason and watermark emission latency.
security_review_summary: Threat modeling completed; main concerns were unsigned endorsements and operator scoping. Changes: signed-by-default endorsements, operator-only management endpoints, audit watermarking to provide tamper-evident records. No P0 vulnerabilities identified.
migration_steps: 1) Roll out rbac_v2_endorsements=false to all clusters. 2) Deploy endorsement schema and migration task to update caches. 3) Enable rbac_v2_endorsements in staging and validate. 4) Enable kms_fallback_guardian in staging, run failure drills. 5) Gradual rollout to prod with monitoring and rollback plan.
testing_summary: Unit coverage added for endorsement rules, guardian scoring graph, and watermark signer. Integration test simulates a primary-region KMS outage and validates that the guardian selects an approved fallback and that watermark entries are emitted and ingested into the audit pipeline.
egress_and_telemetry: New metrics: guardian.fallback_count, guardian.fallback_latency_ms, endorsements.cache_hit_ratio, audit.watermark_emit_ms. Watermark events are sent to internal audit-ingest topic and do not include customer plaintext keys; they include provider IDs and signed assertions.
why_this_is_unique: This PR emphasizes auditable, signed short-lived service endorsements combined with a scoring-based KMS fallback mechanism and a compact signed watermark to tie the whole decision chain together. It focuses on operational traceability during failover rather than only hard residency enforcement, which complements existing region-pin and KMS policies.
